title: Next.js Server Actions & Route Handlers: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on mutating data in the Next.js App Router: Server Actions and forms, cache revalidation, Route Handlers, request/response APIs and middleware, plus when to use each.

chapters.title: Mutation Toolkit Overview
points: Server Action: an async function marked 'use server' that runs on the server and is invoked from forms or client code; Next.js exposes it via a POST endpoint behind the scenes
Route Handler: route.ts exporting GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/HEAD/OPTIONS functions; builds a public HTTP endpoint using Web Request/Response
Middleware: a function that runs before a request completes, matched by path, used to redirect, rewrite, set headers or gate access
Choose Server Action for your own UI's mutations, Route Handler for webhooks, public APIs and non-UI clients, middleware for cross-cutting checks before rendering
A route.ts cannot sit beside a page.tsx at the same route segment; they conflict

chapters.title: Server Actions and Forms
points: Mark a function with 'use server' inline (inside a Server Component) or at the top of a file to export many actions
Pass the action to <form action={fn}>: it receives FormData, so read values with formData.get('name'); forms work before hydration (progressive enhancement)
Always validate input on the server (e.g. with zod) and re-check auth inside the action: actions are public POST endpoints, not private functions
useActionState(action, initialState) returns [state, formAction, pending] for returning validation errors; useFormStatus in a child component reads pending for the submit button
After mutating, call redirect('/path') or revalidate; redirect() throws internally, so never wrap it in try/catch (or call it after the catch)

chapters.title: Revalidation After Mutations
points: revalidatePath('/posts') invalidates the cached data and rendered output for that route on the next visit; pass 'layout' or 'page' as second arg to scope it to a layout or page
revalidateTag('posts') invalidates every fetch/cache entry tagged with that string; tag a fetch with fetch(url, { next: { tags: ['posts'] } })
Path vs tag: path is simple and route-oriented; tag is precise and shared across many routes that use the same data
Call both only from Server Actions or Route Handlers (not during render); use them after the database write succeeds so stale pages refresh
Gotcha: forgetting to revalidate after a mutation leaves the UI showing stale data; revalidating '/' alone does not refresh nested routes unless you use 'layout'

chapters.title: Route Handlers (route.ts)
points: File lives at app/api/items/route.ts (any segment); export named async functions per HTTP method, e.g. export async function GET(request: Request) {...}
Return Response.json(data, { status: 201 }) or new Response(body, { headers }); NextResponse adds helpers like cookies and redirects
Dynamic segments: app/api/items/[id]/route.ts receives the second arg { params }; params is a Promise in recent versions, so await it
Read the body with await request.json() / request.formData() / request.text(); read query with new URL(request.url).searchParams or request.nextUrl.searchParams
Caching gotcha: GET handlers are not cached by default in current versions; opt in with export const dynamic = 'force-static', and reading request or cookies makes it dynamic anyway

chapters.title: Request/Response APIs and Middleware
points: cookies() and headers() from 'next/headers' are async in current versions (await them); cookies().set / delete only work in Server Actions and Route Handlers, not during render
NextRequest extends Request with nextUrl and cookies; NextResponse provides .json(), .redirect(), .rewrite(), .next() for responses
Middleware lives at middleware.ts in project root (or src/) exporting middleware(request) and an optional config = { matcher: ['/dashboard/:path*'] } to limit which paths run it
Typical middleware jobs: auth redirect for protected paths, locale rewrite, adding headers; keep it fast and light, with no heavy DB calls or Node-only APIs on the edge runtime
Don't rely on middleware alone for auth; verify again in Server Actions, Route Handlers and data access, since matchers can miss routes and actions are directly callable

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Which Tool and Key Snippets
points: Decision: own form or button mutation → Server Action; webhook, third-party or mobile client → Route Handler; pre-render redirect, rewrite, header → middleware
Action skeleton: 'use server'; export async function create(prev, formData) { validate; auth check; write DB; revalidatePath('/x'); redirect('/x') }
Handler skeleton: export async function POST(req: Request) { const body = await req.json(); return Response.json({ ok: true }, { status: 201 }) }
Revalidate: revalidatePath('/p', 'layout') for a whole subtree; revalidateTag('t') for tagged fetches; tag via next: { tags: ['t'] }

Middleware skeleton: export function middleware(req) { return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', req.url)) } with config.matcher; checklist: validate, authorize, revalidate, never try/catch redirect
